title: Land Under an Unfamiliar Sky

goal.text: Find your feet on an island high in the sky.

steps.label: Learn to listen for a rift
Help the keeper guard the edge

plate.narration: High above the realm, stone islands drift like slow boats. Gold-roofed temples glow on their backs. Roots dangle into the clouds, and wind banners snap in every direction at once.

island.narration: The fold opens onto dry ground high above the realm. Your party crosses together. Behind you it closes, leaving only cold air. A kitsune temple keeper leads you away from the island's edge. "These are called the Sky Islands," she says. "And this one is not where it belongs." Find shelter, listen for the opening, and help her mark the unsafe path.

variants.text: The Cairnstep griffins bring your whole party across to an island high above the realm. A kitsune temple keeper welcomes you away from the edge. "These are called the Sky Islands," she says. "Our old landing route points into empty sky now." Find shelter, listen for the opening, and help her mark the unsafe path.

lesson.narration: A kitsune named Seren Wisp is comparing notes with a young manticore named Pip Thistledown. They wear the Riftseekers' clasps. "I am finding what has moved," says Pip. Seren asks you to hum the hall note, then listen for an answering sound. "A starweaver can learn to answer a rift's hum. That is called Attune. No one here chooses a rift's rules."

variants.text: A kitsune named Seren Wisp and a manticore named Pip Thistledown are checking another displaced route. Seren asks you to compare the sounds with what she taught you before. Pip adds the new place to his notes.

local.narration: The keeper shows you a rope stretched between two marker posts. Yesterday it pointed toward a neighboring island; now it points into empty sky. A low song sounds beyond the mist. How will you help her keep travelers clear of the edge?

choices.label: Move the warning markers to the path
Listen for the song before marking the path

markers.narration: You move the markers where a traveler will see them before reaching the broken route. The keeper fastens a warning cord between them. "One less person walking toward an old view."

song.narration: You wait until the low song sounds again. It travels through the mist far from the route the keeper expected. You mark that difference on her slate without guessing what it means.

island_rest.narration: The keeper leads you to a sheltered path on the Sky Islands. Beside it stands a stone hut. Its door rattles in the wind. Thump. Something soft hits the wall inside. Far off, a huge shape moves through the mist, singing. You can rest here before following the song.

choices.label: Knock on the stone hut's door
Return to the keeper and set out

island_done.narration: The keeper offers shelter. Far off, a huge shape moves gently through the mist, singing. The party has found new neighbors and a displaced route to investigate.

variants.text: A kitsune captain named Thimble waves from a nearby dock. "Captain Thimble. You found us! The washing is still here." She recognizes you from the Exchange.

dojo.narration: A bigfoot named Master Dunnick opens the door a crack and pulls you in out of the wind. Then he leans his back against it. The wind pushes. He pushes back. He has held this door shut for forty years. "This school is called the Dojo," he says. "Here we train the Thornguard, a hero who holds the line." A thorn bracer hangs on a hook by the fire. A Thornguard's strength lives in that bracer, and a song bell worn beside it will not ring. Thump. In the corner, students are catching pillows as they drop from the rafters. "Anyone who wants the bracer," says Master Dunnick, "may try it on."

variants.text: Master Dunnick is still leaning on the door of the Dojo. "Back already? Good. The wind never stops, so neither do we." The thorn bracer waits on its hook for anyone who wants to try it on. Thump. Another pillow drops.

dojo_pillows.narration: A student unties a rope. Pillows tumble from the rafters. You plant your feet and catch one, then another, then another. The next one lands on your head. Master Dunnick nods without leaving the door. "That is how you brace. Stand still, and let it come to you."

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.
